items.kana: ここわとてもしずかだ

structure_explanation.en: Sentence of the type 「X は Y だ」, which describes the topic. 此処は establishes the topic (this place), とても is an intensity adverb (very), and 静か is a na-adjective (形状詞) meaning silent/quiet. The だ at the end is the casual copula "is", giving the sentence an informal tone.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: Frase do tipo 「X は Y だ」, que descreve o tópico. 此処は estabelece o tópico (este lugar), とても é um advérbio de intensidade (muito) e 静か é um adjetivo な (形状詞) que significa silencioso/tranquilo. O だ no final é a cópula casual "é", dando à frase um tom informal.

translation_literal.en: As for here, it is very quiet.

conjugation_note.en: base form of 静か (na-adjective / 形状詞), used with the copula だ
conjugation_note.pt-BR: forma base de 静か (adjetivo 形状詞/な), usada com a cópula だ

conjugation_note.en: casual だ form of the copula (equivalent to the polite です)
conjugation_note.pt-BR: forma casual だ da cópula (equivale ao です polido)

findings.issue: 此処 uses the non-joyo kanji 此; ここ is written in kana in modern Japanese and in all JLPT materials. Implausible orthography for a course sentence at any level.

items.kana: あついかみにえをえがいた

structure_explanation.en: The sentence follows the basic Japanese order (complements before the verb, which comes last). 厚い紙 is the い-adjective 厚い (thick) directly modifying the noun 紙 (paper). に marks the place where the action takes hold (on the paper), を marks the direct object え (=絵, drawing), and the verb 描く (to draw) comes at the end, in the past form 描いた. Note: the tokenizer labeled え as an interjection, but in context it is 絵 (drawing), the direct object.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A frase segue a ordem japonesa básica (complementos antes do verbo, que vem por último). 厚い紙 é o adjetivo-i 厚い (grosso) modificando diretamente o substantivo 紙 (papel). に marca o lugar onde a ação se fixa (no papel), を marca o objeto direto え (=絵, desenho), e o verbo 描く (desenhar) vem no fim, na forma passada 描いた. Observação: o tokenizador rotulou え como interjeição, mas no contexto é 絵 (desenho), o objeto direto.

translation_literal.en: On thick paper, I drew a drawing.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Em papel grosso, um desenho, (eu) desenhei.

translation.en: I drew on a thick sheet of paper.
translation.pt-BR: Desenhei numa folha de papel grossa.

conjugation_note.en: dictionary form of the い-adjective 厚い, attributive before the noun
conjugation_note.pt-BR: forma de dicionário do adjetivo-i 厚い, atributiva antes do substantivo

conjugation_note.en: stem of the past form of 描く (描い + た)
conjugation_note.pt-BR: raiz da forma passada de 描く (描い + た)

conjugation_note.en: auxiliary た, past form of 描く
conjugation_note.pt-BR: auxiliar た, forma passada de 描く

findings.issue: Inconsistent orthography: the common kanji 絵 is written as kana え while the much harder 描 stays in kanji; natives write 絵を描いた. Kana え invites misparsing (the expl itself apologizes for the tokenizer's confusion).
Internal pipeline commentary ('the tokenizer labeled...') leaked into a learner-facing explanation.
findings.current: Note: the tokenizer labeled え as an interjection, but in context it is 絵 (drawing), the direct object.
findings.proposed: Note: え here is the kana spelling of 絵 (drawing) and is the direct object.

findings.issue: Internal pipeline commentary ('o tokenizador rotulou...') leaked into a learner-facing explanation.
findings.current: Observação: o tokenizador rotulou え como interjeição, mas no contexto é 絵 (desenho), o objeto direto.
findings.proposed: Observação: え aqui é a grafia em kana de 絵 (desenho), o objeto direto.

items.jp: 手の裏を見せてください
items.kana: てのうらをみせてください

structure_explanation.en: The object 手の裏 ('the back of the hand') is marked by を, and the request is formed with the て-form of the verb 見せる ('to show') + ください ('please'). 手の裏 here is tokenized as a single word. The target is the vocabulary 裏 (back/reverse side).
structure_explanation.pt-BR: O objeto 手の裏 ('o verso/dorso da mão') é marcado por を, e o pedido se forma com a forma-て do verbo 見せる ('mostrar') + ください ('por favor'). 手の裏 aqui vem tokenizado como uma única palavra. O alvo é o vocabulário 裏 (parte de trás).

translation_literal.en: Please show me the back of your hand.
translation_literal.pt-BR: O verso da mão mostre, por favor.

translation.en: Please show me the back of your hand.
translation.pt-BR: Mostre as costas da mão, por favor.

conjugation_note.en: て-form of 見せる (見せて), used to form the request with ください
conjugation_note.pt-BR: forma-て de 見せる (見せて), usada para formar o pedido com ください

conjugation_note.en: ください (form of くださる) after the て-form expresses a polite request
conjugation_note.pt-BR: ください (forma de くださる) após a forma-て expressa pedido cortês

findings.issue: 手の裏 does not mean 'back of the hand' (that is 手の甲); dictionaries define 手の裏 as the palm (てのひら). The generated sentence is unnatural and contradicts its own EN/PT translations.
findings.current: 手の裏を見せてください
findings.proposed: 紙の裏を見せてください — and update kana/romaji, en/pt ('the back of the paper'), lit fields, token 手の裏→紙/の/裏, and expl references accordingly.

items.jp: 本をなんさつ借りましたか
items.kana: ほんをなんさつかりましたか

structure_explanation.en: Same structure object + interrogative counter + verb. 本を marks the books as the direct object. The target なん + counter + か is in なんさつ (何冊): なん = 'how many' and さつ (冊) is the counter specific to books and notebooks. 借りました is the polite past of 借りる (to borrow), and か closes the question.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: Mesma estrutura objeto + contador interrogativo + verbo. 本を marca os livros como objeto direto. O alvo なん + contador + か está em なんさつ (何冊): なん = 'quantos' e さつ (冊) é o contador específico para livros e cadernos. 借りました é o passado polido de 借りる (pegar emprestado), e か fecha a pergunta.

translation_literal.en: As for books, how many did you borrow?
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto a livros, quantos volumes (você) pegou emprestado?

translation.en: How many books did you borrow?

conjugation_note.en: connective stem (ます form) of 借りる
conjugation_note.pt-BR: raiz conetiva (forma ます) de 借りる

conjugation_note.en: past form まし of ます
conjugation_note.pt-BR: forma passada まし de ます

findings.issue: Wrong conjugation fact: まし is called the past form of ます. まし is the conjunctive stem (連用形) of ます; the past is carried by the auxiliary た (as the next token itself states). Teaching まし = past is false and internally inconsistent.
findings.current: forma passada まし de ます / past form まし of ます
findings.proposed: raiz conjuntiva (連用形) de ます; o passado vem do auxiliar た / conjunctive stem of ます; past comes from た

structure_explanation.en: Structure: subject + が + traversed space + を + verb of motion. Here を does not mark an ordinary direct object, but the space traversed by the movement (空を翔る = 'to fly across the sky'). 翔る (かける) is a more literary/poetic verb for 'to fly gliding, to soar'. が presents 鳥 as the subject performing the action.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: Estrutura sujeito + が + lugar percorrido + を + verbo de movimento. Aqui を não marca objeto direto comum, mas o espaço atravessado pelo movimento (空を翔る = 'voar atravessando o céu'). 翔る (かける) é um verbo mais literário/poético para 'voar planando, alçar voo'. が apresenta 鳥 como o sujeito que realiza a ação.

translation_literal.en: A bird is flying (gliding) through the sky.

translation.en: The bird flies through the sky.

conjugation_note.en: dictionary (終止形) form of 翔る
conjugation_note.pt-BR: forma de dicionário (終止形) de 翔る

findings.issue: Generated sentence is labeled n4 but uses 翔る (かける), a rare literary/poetic verb outside any JLPT list — the expl itself calls it 'more literary/poetic'. Implausible vocabulary for the claimed level; use 飛ぶ for n4 (or relabel the sentence).
findings.proposed: Fix at vocab level first: retag/deprecate vocab:1570710 翔る as a kana-collision mis-level (community n5 lists meant 掛ける). Then either drop this sentence or regenerate it for the correct lexeme; if a bird-flies sentence is still wanted at n4, use 鳥が空を飛ぶ. Simply swapping 飛ぶ into the existing sentence orphans the 翔る vocab link without fixing the mis-tag.

items.jp: 彼女の毛はとてもきれいだ
items.kana: かのじょのけわとてもきれいだ

structure_explanation.en: Topic + comment: 彼女の毛は establishes the theme (her hair) and きれいだ makes the statement. きれい is a な-adjective (nominal adjective), so it uses だ at the end instead of conjugating like an い-adjective. とても reinforces the degree ('very'). The focus is the vocabulary 毛 (hair/fur).
structure_explanation.pt-BR: Tópico + comentário: 彼女の毛は estabelece o tema (o cabelo dela) e きれいだ faz a afirmação. きれい é um adjetivo-な (adjetivo nominal), por isso usa だ no fim em vez de conjugar como い-adjetivo. とても reforça o grau ('muito'). O foco é o vocabulário 毛 (cabelo/pelo).

translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto ao cabelo dela, é muito bonito.

translation.pt-BR: O cabelo dela é muito bonito.

conjugation_note.en: na-adjective (きれい) used as predicate with だ
conjugation_note.pt-BR: adjetivo-な (きれい) usado como predicado com だ

conjugation_note.en: だ: plain copula (present affirmative), closing the na-adjective
conjugation_note.pt-BR: だ: cópula simples (presente afirmativo), fecha o adjetivo-な

findings.issue: Generated JP is unnatural: bare 毛 for a person's head hair reads as body hair/fur; natives say 髪 or 髪の毛 (彼女の髪はとてもきれいだ). If the target vocab 毛 must stay, switch to an animal subject, e.g. 猫の毛はとてもきれいだ, and update kana/en/pt/tokens.
findings.current: 彼女の毛はとてもきれいだ
findings.proposed: Keep target vocab 毛: rewrite as 猫の毛はとてもきれいだ (kana ねこのけわとてもきれいだ, romaji nekonokewatotemokireida) and update en/pt ('O pelo do gato é muito bonito'), lit_en/lit_pt, expl, and tokens (彼女→猫, gloss 'pelo/fur'). Do NOT replace 毛 with 髪 — that orphans the target vocab link.
